captions.instagram:
On F-1 or J-1 and earned nothing in the US this year? You may still need to file one form.

✔️ Form 8843 is a statement, not a tax bill. It tells the IRS why your days in the US don't count toward residency yet.
✔️ No US income: file Form 8843 by itself. For 2026, that's due June 15, 2027, mailed to the IRS in Austin, TX.
✔️ US wages: attach it to your Form 1040-NR, due April 15, 2027.
✔️ A spouse or child on F-2 or J-2 files their own.

Send this to a friend on F-1.

Source: IRS Form 8843 and Form 1040-NR instructions. Tax information only; for visa or work questions, check with your DSO or an immigration attorney. General information, not advice for your situation.
captions.youtube_title: Earned $0 on F-1? You May Still File Form 8843 (2026 Deadline)
captions.youtube_description: Nonresident students and scholars on F, J, M or Q visas file Form 8843 to exclude their days of presence from the substantial presence test. With no US income, mail Form 8843 by itself by the Form 1040-NR due date: June 15, 2027 for tax year 2026 if you had no wages subject to withholding. With US wages, attach it to Form 1040-NR, due April 15, 2027. Dependents file their own. Source: IRS Form 8843 and Form 1040-NR instructions. Tax information only, not immigration advice.
